concept.name: B-trade
concept.definition: In the A/B/C setup-grading taxonomy used in proprietary trading, a valid playbook setup taken under only partially favorable conditions - worth trading but at reduced size relative to an A-trade. It is the middle tier of the setup-quality hierarchy that links conviction to position size.
concept.intuition: The pattern is right but the context is average - you can play it, just not with A-trade money.
concept.mechanics: A setup meeting playbook definitions but missing some confluence (weaker trend alignment, mediocre volume, suboptimal time of day) is graded B and traded at a fraction of full risk, preserving capital for A opportunities. Per-grade outcome tracking in review keeps the grade boundaries honest.
concept.failure_modes: Under emotional pressure, B-trades get relabeled as A-trades for size, or skipped entirely after losses; both corrupt the sizing logic the taxonomy exists to enforce. B-trades also have thinner expectancy, so execution slippage hurts them proportionally more.
concept.misconceptions: A B-trade is not a bad trade - it is a smaller bet on a positive but lower-expectancy instance. Trading B-setups at full size, not trading them at all, is the common mistake.
concept.example: A clean pullback pattern in a directionless midday tape grades B: tradable at half size because the pattern is right but the context is average.

citations.source: Mike Bellafiore, One Good Trade: Inside the Highly Competitive World of Proprietary Trading (Wiley, 2010) - publisher page
